skill.name: competitors
skill.description: Creates accurate competitor comparison and alternative pages for SEO, buyer education, and product positioning across four common page formats.
skill.summary: Plan and write credible competitor pages with structured research, comparisons, SEO guidance, and migration content.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around file paths and URL examples. The skill contains no shell execution in those locations and no semantic security issue was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format product-marketing file paths as inline Markdown. The line instructs the agent to read an existing context file and contains no shell command.
The backticks format two example URL patterns for a singular alternative page. They are documentation literals, not executable shell syntax.
The backticks format an example URL pattern for a plural alternatives page. No command, interpreter, or execution instruction is present.
The backticks format example comparison-page URL paths. The content is descriptive Markdown and does not invoke Ruby or a shell.
The backticks delimit a competitor comparison URL template. This is a static documentation example with no execution behavior.

content.value_statement: Competitor pages often lack useful detail, balanced claims, and consistent structure. This skill turns verified product data into persuasive comparison content for buyers and search engines.
actual_capabilities: Selects among singular alternative, alternatives roundup, direct comparison, and third-party comparison formats.
Structures pages with summaries, detailed comparisons, pricing, audience fit, migration guidance, and calls to action.
Organizes reusable competitor profiles as a central source for multiple pages.
Plans keyword targeting, URL patterns, internal links, index pages, and page priorities.
Promotes balanced claims by including competitor strengths, product limitations, and evidence from research.
limitations: It does not verify current prices, features, search volume, or customer claims without supplied research.
It does not replace legal review for comparative advertising, trademarks, or disputed claims.
It cannot guarantee search rankings, citations, conversions, or competitor responses.
Internal sales battle cards require a dedicated sales enablement workflow.

use_cases.title: Launch an Alternative Page
use_cases.description: Create a focused page for buyers considering a switch from one named competitor.

use_cases.title: Build a Comparison Content Hub
use_cases.description: Plan reusable competitor data, page formats, URLs, priorities, and internal links across a comparison library.

use_cases.title: Publish an Independent Comparison
use_cases.description: Compare two products objectively with clear criteria, audience recommendations, pricing context, and balanced conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a Direct Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline a comparison page for [Our Product] versus [Competitor]. Our audience is [Audience], and our verified differentiators are [Differentiators].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a structured page outline from basic product context.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Alternative Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a [Competitor] alternative page for [Our Product]. Use only these verified facts: [Facts]. Include pricing, audience fit, migration, and balanced tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a singular alternative page from supplied evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Alternatives Roundup
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a roundup for the keyword [Competitor] alternatives. Compare [Products] using [Criteria], recommend options by use case, and propose internal links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop an SEO roundup that helps readers evaluate several products.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Comparison Hub
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a comparison hub for [Our Product] and [Competitors]. Define centralized research fields, page priorities, URL patterns, cross-links, update owners, and review cadence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a scalable content system for an advanced competitive program.

output_examples.input: Create an outline for Acme versus BetaDesk for small support teams.
output_examples.output: A page outline with a brief verdict, feature and pricing comparisons, team-fit guidance, migration details, evidence notes, and a focused call to action.

output_examples.input: Plan a roundup targeting BetaDesk alternatives.
output: Search intent and evaluation criteria for buyers leaving BetaDesk.
A balanced shortlist with Acme presented first and every option matched to a use case.
Recommended URL, title, comparison table, internal links, and research gaps.

output_examples.input: Design a comparison hub for five project management competitors.
output_examples.output: A prioritized page map, shared competitor profile fields, index structure, cross-linking plan, and quarterly fact-check schedule.

best_practices: Verify every pricing, feature, and customer claim before publication.
Explain which product fits each audience instead of declaring one universal winner.
Store competitor facts centrally and assign a regular update schedule.
anti_patterns: Do not invent competitor weaknesses, reviews, prices, or customer quotes.
Do not publish comparison tables without explaining why each difference matters.
Do not present your product as the best option for every buyer.

faq.question: Which comparison formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports singular alternatives, alternatives roundups, your product versus a competitor, and competitor versus competitor pages.

faq.question: Does the skill research current competitor information?
faq.answer: It provides a research process, but current prices, features, reviews, and search data must be supplied or independently verified.

faq.question: Can it create a complete page draft?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce metadata, section copy, tables, audience guidance, migration content, and calls to action from verified inputs.

faq.question: How does it keep comparisons credible?
faq.answer: It requires balanced strengths, limitations, use cases, and evidence instead of unsupported claims or feature checklists.

faq.question: Can it plan many comparison pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define reusable competitor profiles, page priorities, URL structures, index pages, internal links, and update schedules.

faq.question: Is it suitable for internal sales battle cards?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs internal battle cards and objection handling materials to a dedicated sales enablement workflow.
